sections.h2: Offices that deal with Sauk County property tax
sections.html:
A Sauk County bill passes through three hands. The local assessor values the property. The treasurer of your town, village or city collects the opening payment. The county Treasurer then deals with second installments and anything delinquent, from the West Square Building, 505 Broadway, Room 148, Baraboo, WI 53913. Visit Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or call 608-355-3275.

Valuation in Wisconsin is a municipal job, so the county cannot explain your value. Each taxation district has its own assessor, and the local clerk can name yours. The state's Guide for Property Owners covers the basics.

The county Treasurer page links to Ascent Land Records, an online system for finding a parcel and paying second-installment and delinquent taxes.

Baraboo is the seat of this 849-square-mile rural county, with Reedsburg and Wisconsin Dells (mostly in other counties) as the remaining cities. About 66,652 people lived here in July 2025, in 32,616 housing units. Nearly three in four homes, 72.4%, are owner-occupied. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $258,600, and median household income is $79,541. School district and municipal levies make up much of the bill, so check with the local clerk which ones apply to your parcel.

Your local treasurer gets the first installment, or the entire bill, by January 31. The county Treasurer gets the second by July 31. A rule trips up many owners: an installment must arrive within five working days of its due date, otherwise the whole unpaid balance turns delinquent.

Sauk County installments
PaymentDue datePay to
First installment or full paymentJanuary 31Local treasurer
Second installmentJuly 31Sauk County Treasurer
Delinquent balancesAfter July 31Sauk County Treasurer

Delton, Fairfield, Greenfield and Sumpter allow the first installment to be paid online in the county land records system, at the fees below. Elsewhere, ask your local treasurer how to pay.

  • Credit card: 2.50% of the payment.
  • Debit card: $2.95 flat per transaction.
  • Electronic check: $1.50 per transaction, up to $10,000.

Each month, on the first, an unpaid balance gains 1.5% in interest and penalty. Because one missed installment makes everything remaining delinquent, being late in July puts the whole second half at risk.

Be careful with mail. Postmarks have been applied at regional sorting centers since August 2025, so a letter from a mailbox may show a date several days late, and many state tax deadlines depend on that mark. The county advises handing the envelope to a post office clerk and having it date stamped in front of you.

Expecting to be late? Phone the Treasurer at 608-355-3275 for the exact payoff on your planned payment day.

Start with your assessor. If the number still seems off, your municipality's Board of Review hears the dispute once a year, within 45 days of the fourth Monday in April (s. 70.47). The clerk announces the date and place, so watch for the notice or call in March or April.

  • Open book is first: an informal window when the completed roll is available and the assessor is on hand.
  • Let the clerk know about your objection no later than 48 hours before the board's first meeting.
  • Hand in the written objection form in that meeting's first two hours. For good cause, the board can excuse the notice requirement.
  • Dispute land and improvements together; objecting to just one is not allowed in Wisconsin.
  • After the ruling, the Department of Revenue hears appeals under s. 70.85 for a $100 fee, and circuit court review is open within 90 days.

Section 74.37 offers an excessive assessment claim too. It builds on an earlier Board of Review appeal and has to be written and delivered to the municipality by January 31 of the year the tax comes due.

Phone the Treasurer before anything else, and hold on to each notice you get. Since interest posts on the first of the month, your payoff shifts depending on when you pay. Get the number in writing when a sale or refinance depends on it.

With an escrow account, check that the lender pays on schedule by comparing its yearly statement to the two due dates. Interest applies just the same if the lender pays late.

Wisconsin Help for Homeowners, a state program for overdue housing bills, is listed on the Treasurer page as well. Call 1-855-2-HOME-WI to find out whether it is accepting applications before you build a plan on it.

sections.h2: Selling a Sauk County house with taxes due
sections.html:
Before listing, or before saying yes to an offer, get a payoff from the county Treasurer and send it to the title company. With the first half paid and the second open, the closing agent needs the remaining amount plus interest to date. On a delinquent parcel, interest keeps adding each month.

A completed real estate condition report goes to the buyer on any one to four unit home. Section 709.01 excuses a court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house, a common situation in an estate sale. Anyone who lived there must complete it, and so must a seller whose transfer is not exempt from the transfer fee.

Section E of the form asks about taxes, special assessments and permits, so pull together your latest tax bill, any special assessment notices and your permit records beforehand.

Steps in order: get the payoff, confirm which installments are paid, collect your permit and assessment papers, finish the condition report, and deliver it to the buyer on time after the contract is accepted. A late report gives the buyer a short window to rescind.

When you call the Treasurer's office, have the parcel number and the property address ready, and note the name of the person who gives you the figure. Keep the written payoff with your closing file. If the second installment is still open and the sale will close before July 31, decide in the contract who pays it, and ask the title company to show that split on the closing statement. Sellers with a delinquent parcel should ask the same office how interest is counted through the expected closing date.

A cash buyer may close sooner, yet the tax balance and the disclosure duties are identical.

faqs.q: Who collects Sauk County property tax?
faqs.a: Local treasurers take the first installment or full payment, due January 31. The county Treasurer, at 505 Broadway, Room 148, Baraboo, takes July 31 second installments and every delinquent payment.

faqs.q: How can I pay Sauk County property tax online?
faqs.a: Go to Ascent Land Records, linked from the Treasurer page. Fees are 2.50% for credit cards, $2.95 for debit cards and $1.50 for e-checks up to $10,000. Delton, Fairfield, Greenfield and Sumpter also take first installments there.

faqs.q: What is the late fee on Sauk County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest and penalty of 1.5% are added on the first of every month until the balance is paid. Paying an installment later than five working days after its due date turns the whole remainder delinquent.

faqs.q: Does the county set my Sauk County assessed value?
faqs.a: No, that belongs to your town, village or city assessor. Disputes start with the assessor and move to the municipal Board of Review, which meets within 45 days of the fourth Monday in April.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay Sauk County property tax before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, anything unpaid is cleared at or before closing. The Treasurer can tell you the balance, and the title company pays it from your proceeds. Chapter 709 also requires a condition report unless you qualify for an exemption.
